messages:
Mina Haddad: hey folks — routing team update + question for Support/CS.

Mina Haddad: we’re planning a small set of improvements to fallback metrics + visibility (ties to ENG-4821). goal: during escalations, Support can quickly answer “Are we falling back? to what? why?” without grabbing an eng.

Mina Haddad: current pain we’re seeing in tickets:
- “pinned model/version ignored” (SUP-1847)
- rate-limit/quota confusion when routing shifts (SUP-1843 / SUP-1855)
- customers ask if it’s “regional” but we only have per-service dashboards

Mina Haddad: proposed signals we’ll add/clarify (Support-safe where possible):
1) `routing.fallback_activated` (boolean + count, broken down by region/model/tier)
2) `routing.fallback_reason` (enum: capacity, health, policy, compatibility)
3) `routing.selected_variant` (what we actually served: model + version)
4) `routing.policy_id` (which policy applied; should map to Console config)
5) dashboard panel: “% requests served via fallback” over time, + top reasons

Mina Haddad: question: when you’re in a live escalation, what 3–5 signals would let you triage fastest + write a credible customer update?

Dev Patel: +1 on this. the biggest blocker for us is being able to say “we confirmed fallback is active / not active” and whether it’s expected behavior vs bug.

Dev Patel: top asks from Support side:
- per-region “fallback rate” (so we can answer “is it just eu-west?”)
- “served model + version” vs “requested model + pinned version” (esp. Dedicated/Enterprise)
- a quick way to correlate to request IDs (even if it’s just a log search hint)

Owen Phillips: “why” matters a lot. “capacity” vs “health” changes whether we page SRE and how we message it.

Owen Phillips: also, any chance we can expose something customer-safe in response headers? even just `x-redwood-route: primary|fallback` would cut down a ton of back-and-forth.

Ethan Park: headers might be doable if we’re careful. we already propagate request IDs; adding route metadata is feasible but needs review (don’t want to leak internal topology).

Ethan Park: would `x-redwood-routing: primary` / `x-redwood-routing: fallback` + `x-redwood-fallback-reason: health|capacity` be enough? (no region/cluster details)

Priya Shah: from the trenches — yes. customers already ask for “proof” when they suspect model drift. if we can point them to a header + a KB snippet, it’s copy/paste.

Priya Shah: also please include a very explicit “what to do next” mapping. like:
- fallback_reason=health → check status page / move to #incidents if thresholds hit
- fallback_reason=capacity → involve SRE capacity if Dedicated + sustained >X%
- fallback_reason=policy → verify their Console policy / pinned version

Allison Grant: metrics angle: if you want this to be Support-safe and fast, make the dashboard answer a binary question:
- “Did fallback increase above baseline in the last N minutes?”
- “Is it correlated with 5xx/timeout/latency spikes?”

Allison Grant: suggest a single “Routing / Fallback Overview” dashboard with:
- fallback rate (%) by region
- fallback rate (%) by model family
- p95 latency overlay (same time range)
- error rate overlay
- top fallback reasons table

Sean Gallagher: +1. also please align the thresholds with on-call paging policy. we’ve had cases where Support sees “some fallback” and thinks it’s an incident.

Sean Gallagher: for us, fallback isn’t automatically bad. what matters is:
- does it violate SLOs (latency/availability)
- does it break policy guarantees (pinned version / Dedicated isolation)

Rafael Mendes: +1 from SRE. fallback rate alone can be noise. but “fallback_rate + elevated errors” is a strong escalation trigger.

Mina Haddad: super helpful. summarizing what I’m hearing:
- must-have: fallback rate by region + served model/version vs requested
- must-have: reason code that maps to “what to do next”
- nice-to-have: customer-safe headers indicating primary vs fallback + reason
- must-have: overlay with latency + error rate so Support doesn’t page on normal fallback

Mina Haddad: quick check: in escalations, do you prefer a dashboard link you can paste into the bridge, or a “support command” / bot that answers “is fallback active for request IDs X/Y/Z”?

Dev Patel: dashboard link is quickest for most cases. but if we can do “request id lookup” later, that’s gold for enterprise escalations (cuts cycle time).

Owen Phillips: agree. dashboard first; request ID lookup later. in the meantime, even a runbook note like “search logs for `route_decision` keyed by request id” would help.

Benji Okafor: on implementation: we can add a structured log line at gateway like:
`route_decision request_id=... requested=... served=... fallback=true reason=... policy_id=...`
then build a saved query in our log tool for Support.

Priya Shah: please add this to the Support intake checklist template too (what to ask customers): request IDs + headers. we’re standardizing that anyway.

Ethan Park: re: headers, we’ll need to ensure it’s consistent across streaming + non-streaming + SDKs. but conceptually yes.

Mina Haddad: action items:
- I’ll update ENG-4821 with the specific Support signal requirements + header proposal
- @Allison Grant can you sanity-check the dashboard layout + make sure it’s “support-safe”?
- @Dev Patel/@Owen Phillips if you have 1–2 real examples where this would have changed the customer update, drop the SUP links here

Dev Patel: examples:
- SUP-1847 (pinned model version confusion)
- SUP-1850 (eu-west timeouts — we spent too long proving it was regional + not customer networking)

Owen Phillips: also SUP-1842 streaming resets in us-east — even though it’s not purely routing, we got asked “are we being routed around something”. having fallback panels in the bridge would’ve helped.

Rafael Mendes: +1 on “bridge paste”. if we can standardize a single link to “Fallback Overview” it becomes part of the escalation template.

Mina Haddad: perfect. will propose a canonical dashboard link and we can get it added to the bridge template/runbook (ENG-4823-ish). thanks all — keep feedback coming as you hit cases.
